q1_issues.issue: The clause is explicitly past ("Last year, there were shortages") but no shortage witness carries a (Past ...) atom, so the shortages are left unmarked, which the instruction set defines as generic/habitual.

"shots" and "shortages" are plurals but each is encoded as a singular witness ((Member sk_shot_1 shot), (Member sk_shortage_1 shortage)) rather than the group witness (GroupOf <g> <kind>) the instruction set requires for a plural.

"nationally" is an -ly adverb, not a place NP, so (Location sk_shortage_1 nationally) fills a role the instruction set glosses as "in/at/on ..." (whose object follows ordinary NP rules) with an adverb that the -ly rule keeps in surface form.

q2_gaps: a scope/domain -ly adverb ("nationally") saying over what territory a claim holds: the instruction set gives -ly adverbs the Manner slot and Location a preposition-headed PP, but nothing for an adverb of geographic scope
notes: Replicating the whole predication five times over the coordinated "for"-list is a defensible reading of the distributive default, and For/Of on the noun symbols are the licensed argument obliques. Time and Location on sk_shortage_N are only licensed if "shortage" counts as an event-denoting noun (the witness IS the eventuality); the parse relies on that without it being settled.
